title: Existence of a computing resolution pairing
statement: For any scheme X and module sheaves F,G on X, there exists a CupResolutionPairing F G [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data]. No cohomological degree, flatness or quasi-coherence hypothesis is required. This asserts only the existence of three computing resolutions and a sectionwise tensor chain pairing, not a cup product on cohomology or its uniqueness.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.31; Lemma 20.31.3 and the flasque-resolution proof of Lemma 20.31.4 (Tag 0FKV)

proof.text: Take the existential nonnegative integer complexes K,L,M, their quasi-isomorphic augmentations and total tensor cochain map from moduleCup_godement_pairing; no specified or natural Godement model is assumed by this lemma. Restrict the complexes to natural degrees using their strictly nonnegative support. On each tensor summand and open, compose tensoring sections with the summand inclusion and the supplied cochain map. The cochain-map equation gives signed Leibniz, sheaf morphisms give restriction compatibility, and the degree-zero equation gives augmentation compatibility.

The supplied terms are flasque and the supplied augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Extend each augmentation to a comparison with an injective resolution degree by degree. Use moduleCup_flasque_acyclicity for the terms, then the separately cited Leray acyclic-resolution criterion to show that global comparison homology maps are isomorphisms. Assemble the three computing resolutions and their section pairing into CupResolutionPairing.

proof_origin.place: Proof of the acyclic-resolution characterization, extracted from the item docstring and Section 20.31
